explanation: Procopius says the emperor Justinian sent them to fetch the secret of silk. The eggs let Byzantium start its own silk industry, cutting its reliance on imports through Persia.

claims.text: The historian Procopius reports that in the 550s monks smuggled silkworm eggs into the Byzantine Empire hidden in hollow canes.
The story concerns silkworm eggs, not tea, pepper or cotton seeds.
According to Procopius, Justinian encouraged the monks, with promises of reward, to bring silkworms from the east.
Before this, Byzantium bought raw silk largely through Persian intermediaries, and afterwards it developed its own silk production.
